commitments.text: Fibreco must cause the Project to be designed, located, constructed, operated, dismantled or abandoned in accordance with documents listed in Schedule A to this Project approval certificate.

Fibreco must cause all intersection improvements as outlined in section 5.3.1 of the Delcan Engineers/Planners Traffic Impact Study for the Fibreco Pulp Mill Extension, Taylor, BC, dated September, 1995, to be undertaken, and Fibreco must bear the cost of those improvements; the intersection improvements must be completed in accordance with all applicable acts, regulations, permits, licenses, approvals, standards or other relevant authorities.

Fibreco must: (a) prepare written reports to the reasonable satisfaction of the Director of the Policy Development Branch, Ministry of Employment and Investment, on the progress of commitments made by Fibreco to prevent or reduce socioeconomic impacts resulting from the Project; (b) include the following matters in the reports: (i) the schedule for construction of the Project, (ii) the hiring schedule for the Project, (iii) hiring and employment statistics relating to the Project, (iv) the steps taken by Fibreco to support hiring of people resident in the Taylor area, (v) statistics regarding the location of the residences of new employees, (vi) the steps taken by Fibreco to communicate with aboriginal people regarding employment opportunities, (vii) statistics on numbers of aboriginal people employed by Fibreco, and (viii) consultations between Fibreco and the RCMP, local school boards and local health agencies regarding potential socioeconomic impacts of the Project.
